rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The theme that is secretly about time A hobby is what you do when nobody is making you do anything — which is why the theme, lightly examined, turns out to be about identity, discipline and joy. The exam likes it because every candidate has material: the football at dawn, the guitar with two broken strings, the novel abandoned at page forty.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Hobbies develop skills and identity — argue their value beyond entertainment.
Use hobby vocabulary (collecting, crafting, trekking) naturally in sentences.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ## The debates, held honestly **"Are hobbies a waste of time?"** Concede the opportunity cost honestly — an hour of guitar is an hour not studied. Rebut with the evidence of how attention works: a rested, pleased mind learns faster than an exhausted one; the hobby is not theft from study but interest paid on it.…  ·  ## Grammar and style: the tense of habit Hobbies live in the **present simple with adverbs of frequency** — "I **usually** sketch on Saturdays", "We **hardly ever** miss the morning match" — and the exam quietly checks the position of those adverbs (before the main verb, after *be*).…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## How the exam asks it The **personal essay** ("My hobby", 6–8 marks) wants one hobby deep, not five hobbies listed: what, when, how it began, one anecdote, what it taught. The **dialogue** (two friends on free time) wants turn-taking, gerunds flying free, and one recommendation with a reason. The **short answers** want the verb-pattern rules said with examples.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. Why are hobbies important for students? (2 marks) — stress relief and skill-building; one concrete example.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Q. Describe a hobby of yours and what it has taught you. (3 marks) — specific activity, routine, one lesson learned.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The words that carry the theme The verb **to go** splits the theme neatly: you **go swimming, go trekking, go fishing** (go + -ing for activities away from home), but you **play** chess and **collect** stamps and **read** novels — the collocations are fixed, and mixing them ("I go chess") is the theme's signature error.…  ·  ## Reading the theme like a writer — writing pleasure well Writing about a hobby fails in one specific way: **the brochure voice** — "Reading is very interesting and improves knowledge." The cure is the same concrete detail that carried the family and sports units: not "I love trekking" but "the tea house at 4,000 metres, where the owner's daughter does homework by lantern and the fog closes like a curtain at…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: 'Describe your hobby' answers need SPECIFICS: when you started, what you actually do, one skill gained — concrete detail is the band marker.  ·  Trick 2: Argue the value line: hobbies build skills and mental health — connect one hobby to one benefit, not a generic list.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. Describe a hobby of yours and what it has taught you. (3 marks) — specific activity, routine, one lesson learned.
